summary: Derm Foundation is a machine learning model designed to accelerate AI development for skin image analysis in dermatology applications. It generates 6144-dimensional embeddings from skin images, enabling efficient training of AI models with less data and compute [SOURCE 3].
intended_use_and_workflow: Derm Foundation can reduce the data, compute, and expertise needed to develop task-specific models for skin image analysis.  It can be used to classify clinical conditions, score severity, identify body parts, and determine image quality [SOURCE 3, SOURCE 1].
model_limitations: Derm Foundation's quality can degrade in extreme lighting conditions. It was trained on data from a limited set of countries (US, Colombia, Australia) and may not generalize well to other countries, patient populations, or image types [SOURCE 3]. It also doesn't make predictions or diagnoses [SOURCE 3].
model_type: The model is a BiT-101x3 CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) [SOURCE 3]. It's a machine learning model that produces embeddings based on dermatology images [SOURCE 1].
foundation_models_used_in_application_if: Derm Foundation uses a BiT ResNet-101x3 architecture and was pre-trained on a wide range of skin images to produce enriched embeddings useful for data-efficient classification of skin related tasks. It also uses image-text pairs from the internet.
training_data: The model was trained in two stages: first, using contrastive learning on public image-text pairs, and then fine-tuned for condition classification using clinical datasets [SOURCE 5, SOURCE 3]. Datasets included teledermatology data from the US and Colombia, a skin cancer dataset from Australia, and additional public images [SOURCE 3].
validation_test_dataset: Derm Foundation was evaluated for data-efficient accuracy across skin-related classification tasks.  Training a linear classifier on Derm Foundation's embeddings was more performant than using a standard BiT-M model [SOURCE 3].
